title: History 2: Variational autoencoders and the latent idea (2013)

questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between a standard Autoencoder (AE) and a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) in terms of their mapping to latent space?
options: AE maps to a distribution, VAE maps to a single point
AE maps to a single point, VAE maps to a distribution
AE uses stochastic sampling, VAE uses deterministic mapping
AE compresses data, VAE expands data
questions.answer: AE maps to a single point, VAE maps to a distribution
questions.why: The lesson states that an AE maps an input to a fixed vector (a point), whereas a VAE maps an image to a distribution (a cloud of possibilities).

questions.q: In the VAE reparameterization trick, what is the formula used to calculate the latent vector z?
questions.why: The lesson explicitly defines the reparameterization trick formula as z = mu + epsilon * sigma, where epsilon is drawn from a standard normal distribution.

questions.q: Why is the KL Divergence Loss included in the VAE loss function?
options: To maximize the sharpness of the reconstructed images
To force the latent space to be smooth and centered around zero
To increase the dimensionality of the latent vector
To prevent the decoder from reconstructing the input
questions.answer: To force the latent space to be smooth and centered around zero
questions.why: The lesson explains that the KL Divergence Loss forces the latent distribution to look like the prior (standard normal), which ensures the latent space is smooth and centered around zero.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what happens to the latent space if the KL Divergence Loss is removed from the VAE training?
questions.answer: The latent space becomes disjointed, and you will not be able to interpolate between images.
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section states that ignoring the KL Loss causes the latent space to become disjointed, preventing interpolation between images.

questions.q: In the provided lab results, what does the value `RESULT mu_shape = [8, 2]` indicate about the encoder's output?
options: The batch size is 2 and the latent dimension is 8
The encoder outputs a mean vector of dimension 2 for each of the 8 samples
The input data has a dimensionality of 8 and 2
The standard deviation is calculated for 8 dimensions
questions.answer: The encoder outputs a mean vector of dimension 2 for each of the 8 samples
questions.why: The lesson explicitly interprets `RESULT mu_shape = [8, 2]` as confirming that the encoder outputs a mean vector of dimension 2 for each of the 8 samples in the batch.
